## MaxPerson (MAXGEN 2.1 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxperson/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/person.schema.json  SHA-256 33a42e40d29768874c1def2ba9823bc28455a614bf18efe5a0bfb452f2dee700
One MaxPerson is one person, as a researched conclusion (holds no family links).

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxPerson is one person as a researched conclusion, every fact about them a claim citing one piece of evidence, holding no family links (parents, children and partners live in MaxRelationship).

### Fields

- person_id (uuid, required): This person's permanent random id, created once by the writer and never recomputed or reused.
- person_kind (enum): Whether this is a documented person or a placeholder made only so something (a parent link, a DNA hypothesis, a death) can attach to them; never created under an import task (R-23).
- placeholder_label (string): Plain words saying who a placeholder stands for, such as "unknown father of Mabel's three daughters"; required when person_kind is placeholder.
- is_living (boolean, required): Living A: whether this person may be alive, with no default (unsure means true); true requires tier2-private, it is a floor that only rises, and privacy is always worked out again when read.
- redistribution_license (licence, required): Whether this person's document may be shared, and under what licence; must be tier2-private while is_living is true.
- outside_ids: refused by name (a document that contains it is not valid)
- name_assertions (array of name_claim): Name claims, each citing its evidence; at least one is required unless person_kind is placeholder.
- gender_assertions (array of gender_claim): Gender claims, each keeping the document's own words.
- birth_assertions (array of vital_claim): Claims about this person's own birth, always with role principal (another person's part at a birth goes in event_assertions).
- death_assertions (array of death_claim): Claims about this person's own death, always with role principal (another person's part at a death goes in event_assertions).
- event_assertions (array of event_claim): Other events in this person's life and their roles at other people's events; a couple event with role principal, bride, groom, spouse or partner is refused here because it is a family fact written with link (R-22).
- attribute_assertions (array of attribute_claim): Lasting facts such as occupation, residence or religion, each citing its evidence.
- non_event_assertions (array of non_event_claim): Claims that something did not happen, such as no marriage by a stated date (GEDCOM 7 NO).
- membership_assertions (array of membership_claim): Membership of a historical group, each citing this person's own line on a roster or similar record (MaxGroup keeps no member list).
- photo_assertions (array of photo_claim): Claims that a face or figure on a photograph record is this person.
- external_id_assertions (array of external_id_claim): Claims that this person is the same as a profile in another system; the only place an outside id for a person is recorded.
- attached_sources (array of attached_source): Records another program attached to this person without naming a fact; research pointers only, never evidence.
- same_as_candidates (array of same_as_candidate): People who may be the same as this one but are not merged (GEDCOM 7 ALIA); a merge still needs the merge_person path.

### Example (made up; birth_calculated_from_census_age.json)

```json
{
  "person_id": "2a946e38-5769-5fdc-b888-e67cc4b40342",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "is_living": false,
  "redistribution_license": "CC0",
  "name_assertions": [
    {
      "name_as_written": "Mossbury, Amos",
      "given_name": "Amos",
      "surname": "Mossbury",
      "confidence": 0.9,
      "task_id": "f1f1f427-edc8-59ac-b068-c44d0daf5f82",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "325d904c-1f07-52ff-85d2-856cb65a60cd",
        "mention_id": "11",
        "record_event_ref": "e1",
        "quote": "Mossbury, Amos",
        "kind": "direct"
      }
    }
  ],
  "birth_assertions": [
    {
      "date": {
        "modifier": "about",
        "value": {
          "year": 1896
        },
        "derivation": "calculated",
        "derivation_note": "age 44 on the 1940 census day"
      },
      "age_as_written": "44",
      "confidence": 0.6,
      "task_id": "f1f1f427-edc8-59ac-b068-c44d0daf5f82",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "325d904c-1f07-52ff-85d2-856cb65a60cd",
        "mention_id": "11",
        "record_event_ref": "e1",
        "quote": "Mossbury, Amos | Head | M | 44",
        "kind": "indirect"
      }
    }
  ],
  "attribute_assertions": [
    {
      "attribute_type": "occupation",
      "value_as_written": "Miller",
      "occurrence_id": "8a37321b-3688-589b-8d1a-1a596a352edb",
      "confidence": 0.85,
      "task_id": "f1f1f427-edc8-59ac-b068-c44d0daf5f82",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "325d904c-1f07-52ff-85d2-856cb65a60cd",
        "mention_id": "11",
        "record_event_ref": "e1",
        "quote": "Miller",
        "kind": "direct"
      }
    }
  ],
  "created_by_task_id": "f1f1f427-edc8-59ac-b068-c44d0daf5f82",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

**Holds no family links.** Removed: `parent_assertions`, `child_assertions`,
`spouse_assertions` (to MaxRelationship); `composite_confidence` (a stored score);
`external_ids` (a mirror); `dna_evidence` (DNA is cited through the evidence link);
`place_registry` (to MaxPlace); `source_record_ids` (an index); `occupation_assertions` (now
`attribute_assertions` with `attribute_type: occupation`); `asserted_by`, `asserted_at`,
`last_updated_at`, `judge_approved`, `judge_approved_at` (task provenance, kit timestamps and
the database's review stage); `merge_status` (now `lifecycle`); the flat date keys and
`country_code`/`state_province` (now the date and place blocks). Changed: every claim gains the
claim header and an evidence link; photo claims point at a photograph record. Added:
`person_kind` and `placeholder_label`, attribute, non-event and group-membership claims,
`name_parts` and `name_status`, `attached_sources`, `same_as_candidates`. `is_living` and
`redistribution_license` become required, with no default; `name_assertions` is required for a
documented person.

### Added in 2.1

- attribute_claim.attribute_type: new allowed value health_condition
- attribute_claim.attribute_type (description updated): What kind of lasting fact this is; health_condition (MAXGEN 2.1) is a health condition as written, private by default and never shared.

### Listen

Episode 2, MaxPerson — The person who might be your ancestor (22:46): https://opengenealogyai.org/podcasts/audio/MAXGEN-02-maxperson-v2.mp3 — Assertions not facts, probabilistic parents, composite confidence, and the merge model. It describes MAXGEN v1.11; see https://opengenealogyai.org/changelog/#v20-2026-10-16 for what changed since.

## MaxRelationship (MAXGEN 2.1 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxrelationship/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/relationship.schema.json  SHA-256 3fe0a82b950eb6fa5b501258cf50c9b41894f7f41039051a16170cc5c5af5d5d
One MaxRelationship is one family link, stored once: a `family`, a `parent_child` pair or an `association`.

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- one family link stored once: a family (a union, household or parent set with its child memberships), one parent and child pair with its lineage facts, or a standing association between two people. Agents never write these files by hand: the helper's link command finds or creates them, and only import_file, resolve_conflict and build_tree tasks may add one directly (R-24). MaxPerson keeps no copy of any link and there is no two-sided lock.

### Fields

- relationship_id (uuid, required): This link's permanent id: a random UUID created once by the helper's link command (or by the importer or analysis task that adds it), never computed from the people's ids and never reused.
- kind (enum, required): Which of the three kinds of link this document is (family, parent_child or association); each kind forbids the other kinds' fields, and a document of an unknown kind is refused at write and skipped with a warning at read
- is_living_flag (boolean, required): Living A floor, required with no default: true when a person this link names may be alive (a family: either partner only, since each child is judged on its own membership; a parent_child record: the parent or the child; 
- redistribution_license (licence, required): Licence of this link, set by the helper to the strictest of the people it names and the records its claims cite (a family: the partners and the records its family facts cite) and raised later but never lowered; a true is
- media_refs (array of media_ref): Photographs of the couple or the family, pointing at saved copies that are described once on the records that captured them.
- partners (array of partner): Family only: zero to two live partner items, unordered, each either a person or an absent partner whom a document mentions without naming; absent and person items both count toward the two, retracted items stay stored an
- union_type (enum): Family only: the importing program's (or the writer's) word for the kind of union, kept as given, unknown when nothing says; never shown when the family has live family facts, which are the only evidence of a union; shar
- union_type_as_written (string): Family only: the documents' or the other program's own words for the union, kept when union_type is other or when the words say more.
- union_type_uri (uri): Family only: a published vocabulary's address for the union type, when one exists.
- fact_assertions (array of family_fact_claim): Family only: facts about the couple or household (marriage, banns, licence, divorce, a census showing them as husband and wife ...), each one claim citing one piece of evidence and held by the partner set.
- non_event_assertions (array of non_event_claim): Family only: things the evidence says did not happen to this couple (GEDCOM 7 NO), each one claim with the same shape as MaxPerson's; an undated one never counts toward the living test or date bounds.
- children (array of membership): Family only: each child's place in this parent set; a child may hold two memberships in one family only when their set kinds differ, because there is one live membership per child, family and set kind (R-20).
- parent_id (uuid): Parent_child only: the parent person, resolved through merge redirects when read; there is exactly one live parent_child record per parent and child pair (R-20).
- child_id (uuid): Parent_child only: the child person, resolved through merge redirects when read; it must differ from parent_id (R-06).
- parent_role (enum): Parent_child only: the parent's role as the documents show it, unknown until a document says; a later father-versus-mother conflict is refused by the helper for an analysis task to settle.
- parent_role_as_written (string): Parent_child only: the parent's own words on the record, such as Head or father, never the child's words.
- lineage_assertions (array of lineage_claim): Parent_child only: at least one lineage fact saying what kind of parent this person is to this child, each judged on its own evidence; one man who is both birth father and adoptive father has one record holding two facts
- association_type (enum): Association only: the kind of standing tie, with this direction: godparent -- party1 is the godparent; enslaved_by -- party1 is the enslaved person and party2 the enslaver; ancestor_descendant -- party1 is the ancestor; 
- association_type_as_written (string): Association only: the document's or the other program's own words for the tie, kept when association_type is other or when the words say more.
- association_type_uri (uri): Association only: a published vocabulary's address for the association type, when one exists.
- generations (integer): Association only, and only with association_type ancestor_descendant: how many generations separate party1 (the ancestor) from party2, when known.
- party1 (party): Association only: the first party; for a directed type it is the godparent, the enslaved person, the ancestor or the employer.
- party2 (party): Association only: the second party; for a directed type it is the godchild, the enslaver, the descendant or the employee.
- association_assertions (array of association_claim): Association only: at least one claim that the tie existed, began or ended, each citing one piece of evidence.

### Example (made up; parent_child_candidate_father_a.json)

```json
{
  "relationship_id": "c967855d-e512-5c3c-8084-aa1c3439e312",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "kind": "parent_child",
  "is_living_flag": false,
  "redistribution_license": "CC0",
  "parent_id": "fed1f33a-d9b4-51f2-9d73-d97aee90c2b4",
  "child_id": "65feecf1-edc0-53b0-8a07-facdedecc81b",
  "parent_role": "father",
  "parent_role_as_written": "reputed father",
  "lineage_assertions": [
    {
      "assertion_id": "7d437c4d-f926-5e5d-907f-d8240e0c8b20",
      "fact_type": "birth_parent",
      "parent_mention_id": "m3",
      "child_mention_id": "m1",
      "confidence": 0.6,
      "task_id": "321dd029-e1b0-5335-814f-37fd6711f5bb",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "cbbbabf3-db47-51a4-8001-88c4e784c88a",
        "mention_id": "m1",
        "record_event_ref": "e1",
        "quote": "Pip, base son of Dorcas Bramblecott, singlewoman; reputed father Ned Mossbury",
        "kind": "direct"
      }
    }
  ],
  "created_by_task_id": "321dd029-e1b0-5335-814f-37fd6711f5bb",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

Every family link, stored once. Three kinds: **`family`** (0 to 2 partners — a person, or an
"absent" partner the document mentions without naming — family facts such as marriage, banns,
divorce or a census together, and child memberships, each with a `set_kind`: `birth`,
`adoptive`, `step_household`, `foster`, `guardianship`, `sealing`, `alternative_hypothesis`,
`other`, a `child_order` and a kit-computed `is_preferred`); **`parent_child`** (one per parent
and child, with lineage facts such as `birth_parent`, `adoptive_parent`, `step_parent`, each
with a dimension: genetic, gestational, legal, social, religious, household, unknown, other); and
**`association`** (godparent, enslaved by, ancestor-descendant, employer, neighbour, friend,
multiple birth, other). No two-sided lock: MaxPerson keeps no copy of any link. A child can belong to
several parent sets, so an adopted person can trace both their birth and their adoptive
lineage. Agents never write these files: the kit's `link` command finds or makes them. Replaces
1.13's `parent_assertions`, `child_assertions`, `spouse_assertions`, `relationship_type` on
parents and the `ecclesiastical` type.

### Listen

No episode yet: MaxRelationship is new in MAXGEN 2.0.


---
## MaxTask (MAXGEN 2.1 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxtask/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/task-queue.schema.json  SHA-256 0a5d2354506e81bc336cefe3b9af5c387fd5f4e83dc8b255f4e274586ecef457
One MaxTask is one piece of work: research, an import, a review or a proof.

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxTask is the permanent record of one piece of work done in a database (research, an import, a review or a proof), never pruned while anything points at it.

### Fields

- task_id (uuid, required): This task's own id: a random UUID created once by the writer and never reused.
- created_by_task_id: refused by name (a document that contains it is not valid)
- task_type (enum, required): What kind of work this is; a task of type other permits none of the gated actions of rules R-24, R-28 and R-31.
- task_type_as_written (string): The kind of work in the writer's own words, given when task_type is other.
- status (enum, required): Where the work stands, changed only through the helper's task command (pending, processing, then done, failed or escalated; on_hold pauses it; a task made by mistake or retracted is cancelled, never deleted).
- priority (integer): How urgent the task is, from 1 (lowest) to 10 (highest).
- payload (object): The task's input, an open object whose documented kinds are interview, person_request, person_page_session, fan_survey (person_id), run (run_id, on a judge_review task), find_original (record_id), import_file (format: ge
- result (result): What the work found and decided, in a closed, readable shape.
- provenance (provenance): Helper-owned and written once: who did the work of this task, filled when the task is first claimed (moved to processing) or created already done.
- created_by (string): The agent id of the session that wrote this task: optional in input, filled by the helper from the writing session, required in stored form, and a different value is refused (R-14).
- started_at (timestamp): Helper-owned: when the task was first moved to processing.
- completed_at (timestamp): Helper-owned: when the task reached done, failed or cancelled.
- is_living_flag (boolean, required): Living A floor: true when the task names or concerns someone who may be alive (unsure means true); it only rises, and while it is true the task must be first_party_only.
- contributor_eligibility (enum): Who may be given this task: first_party_only (the person's own kit and agents, the default, failing closed) or any_contributor; it must be first_party_only whenever is_living_flag is true.
- assigned_to (string): The agent id now working on this task; absent while it is pending.
- cost_usd (number): What the work actually cost, in US dollars.
- cost_cap_usd (number): The most this task may cost, in US dollars; the agent stops and escalates before going over it.
- retry_count (integer): How many times the task has been retried after a failure.
- max_retries (integer): How many retries are allowed before the task is left failed.
- error_message (string): What went wrong, when the task failed or was escalated.
- escalation_reason (string): Why the task was escalated for a further decision.
- queue_file_path (string): The task's path in a file-based queue on this computer; private, never exported.
- depends_on (array of uuid): Tasks that must be done before this one can start.
- parent_task_id (uuid): The task that made this task (on MaxTask this replaces created_by_task_id, which tasks may not carry).
- acceptance_criteria (array of string): Plain, checkable conditions that a complete result must meet.
- min_confidence (confidence): The lowest result confidence that can be accepted.
- evidence_required (array of string): What the worker must hand back as proof of the work (addresses, exact queries, records saved).
- deadline (timestamp): When the work should be finished.

### Example (made up; extract_record_with_steps.json)

```json
{
  "task_id": "79f310ff-0478-5af4-abc5-f6316de4cffb",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "task_type": "extract_record",
  "status": "done",
  "payload": {
    "kind": "extract",
    "person_id": "0aacaa81-8ca0-5df6-8ff8-2a9f7067d76f"
  },
  "result": {
    "hypothesis_tested": "Mabel was baptised at Tumblebrook in 1924.",
    "what_we_did_and_result": "Searched two collections; found the baptism entry; one site needed a login.",
    "steps": [
      {
        "step_no": 1,
        "action": "search",
        "source": "Tumblebrook parish registers (made-up online images)",
        "source_id": "75df6185-5f2f-5652-afb4-fb6349ea015f",
        "source_url": "https://records.example.org/sample/tumblebrook-baptisms",
        "query": "Thistlewood baptisms 1920-1930",
        "coverage": {
          "span": {
            "modifier": "from_to",
            "value": {
              "year": 1920
            },
            "value2": {
              "year": 1930
            },
            "derivation": "interpreted"
          },
          "place": {
            "place_as_written": "Tumblebrook"
          },
          "record_types": [
            "parish_register"
          ]
        },
        "found": "one entry: Mabel, baptised 16 March 1924",
        "record_id": "d990b9d1-f418-573b-83e7-21792a44085d",
        "person_id": "0aacaa81-8ca0-5df6-8ff8-2a9f7067d76f",
        "verdict": "key_finding",
        "confidence": 0.95,
        "at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z"
      },
      {
        "step_no": 2,
        "action": "search",
        "source": "Erewhon civil birth index (made up)",
        "source_url": "https://index.example.org/births",
        "query": "Thistlewood births 1924",
        "found": "The site asked for a login. Not searched; agents never handle passwords.",
        "verdict": "inaccessible",
        "at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z"
      }
    ],
    "verdict": "usable",
    "verdict_reason": "the baptism entry was found and transcribed",
    "confidence": 0.9
  },
  "is_living_flag": false,
  "contributor_eligibility": "first_party_only",
  "provenance": {
    "agent_id": "db:99a01bf5-fdde-51dc-af11-eef027d87f5b/Genealogist",
    "agent_kind": "ai",
    "role": "Genealogist",
    "party": "db:99a01bf5-fdde-51dc-af11-eef027d87f5b",
    "run_id": "r1",
    "display_name": "Genealogist",
    "model": {
      "provider": "example",
      "name": "fixture-model",
      "attested_by": "self_reported"
    },
    "claimed_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
    "channel": "cli"
  },
  "created_by": "db:99a01bf5-fdde-51dc-af11-eef027d87f5b/Genealogist",
  "started_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-10-16T12:30:00Z",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

Removed: `contributor` (now `provenance`, written once by the kit), the top-level `review`
(reviews are now separate `judge_review` tasks, never overwritten), a required `created_at`
(now kit-owned). Added: `provenance`, `is_living_flag` (required), statuses `on_hold` and
`cancelled`, task types `find_original` and `import_file`, the verdict `inaccessible` (could
not search; never a dead end), and a closed `result` holding the search steps (the only search
log), a proof write-up (the single authority for "proven"), occurrence verdicts, reviews, run
decisions and FAN-club associates (the friends, associates and neighbours studied around one
person). A proof's parent-set changes can set a set's kind, make it the main set, add a
parent's existing link to it, or retract it.

### Added in 2.1

- payload.kind (description updated): Which documented payload this is: interview, person_request, person_page_session, fan_survey, run, find_original, import_file, analysis, or (G-04, additive) incoming_finding: one finding from another tree (a relative's file as suggestions, a findings delivery), holding its proposed facts and any proposed new person in the payload (sender_tree_id, sender_label, received_at, verdict, person_id or new_person and relation, facts) until the person lets it in; it is never a claim on the person's people while it waits.

Episode 3, MaxTask — Distributing the work (24:29): https://opengenealogyai.org/podcasts/audio/MAXGEN-03-maxtask.mp3 — Task types, the verdict vocabulary, acceptance criteria, and the anti-hallucination rule. It describes MAXGEN v1.11; see https://opengenealogyai.org/changelog/#v20-2026-10-16 for what changed since.

## MaxSource (MAXGEN 2.1 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxsource/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/source.schema.json  SHA-256 c46fe41a47a681c20634e00d616a31e084db4ba807bac0a80ee58d284f5d6a16
One MaxSource is one work, collection or repository.

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxSource is one work, collection or repository that documents come from or are held by (a book, a periodical, a census collection, a microfilm publication, a family Bible, an archive, a library or a website), with what it covers and how to search it.

### Fields

- source_id (uuid, required): This source's own id: a random UUID created once by the writer and never reused.
- name (string, required): The source's name in plain words, such as a made-up 'Tumblebrook parish registers, 1801-1900'.
- source_type (enum, required): What kind of source this is.
- source_type_as_written (string): The kind of source in the writer's or the other program's own words, given when source_type is other.
- redistribution_license (licence, required): Whether this source entry may be shared (unclear means ask, never guess); a tier2-private entry never appears in any open dataset, share, export, public embedding or commit.
- is_living_flag (boolean, required): Living A floor: true when this source entry names someone who may be alive, such as a privately held family Bible (unsure means true; credits never set it); true requires tier2-private.
- source_url (uri): The source's own address, when it has one; optional (a book or a family Bible has none) and never invented.
- address (place_ref): MAXGEN 2.1 (G-14): where an archive or library is: its postal address in address_as_written, its town in place_as_written, and the MaxPlace in place_id; only on a source whose source_type is archive or library, or other 
- parent_source_id (uuid): The larger MaxSource this one is part of, such as the collection that holds this series.
- description (text): What this source holds and who it serves, in plain words.
- embedding_text (text): Plain text built from the name, description and coverage, for search indexes.
- bibliographic (bibliographic): How the work is cited: title, creators, publisher and edition.
- holdings (array of holding): The repositories that hold this source, with call numbers.
- coverage (coverage): What the source covers, including, for each place, which years it holds and the exact words to search with (routing lives only here).
- access (access): How the source is reached, and the polite way to search it.
- link_status (enum): Whether the source's address still works; a dead link is marked, never deleted.
- last_verified_at (timestamp): When the address was last confirmed to work.
- discovered_via (enum): How this source entry was first found.
- discovered_via_as_written (string): How it was found, in the writer's own words, given when discovered_via is other.
- external_ref (string): The link, category path or article title where this entry was found.
- attribution (attribution): Credit to the human who compiled or contributed this entry (a credit never sets the living flag).
- media_refs (array of media_ref): Files that show this source (a title page, a repository photograph), each described once on the record that captured it.

### Example (made up; census_collection_with_routing.json)

```json
{
  "source_id": "2a140cc7-1211-5c72-8071-ccd81e1ddcc7",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "name": "Erewhon census of 1940 (made up)",
  "source_type": "census_collection",
  "redistribution_license": "CC0",
  "is_living_flag": false,
  "source_url": "https://records.example.org/sample/census-1940",
  "holdings": [
    {
      "repository_name": "Erewhon National Archive (made up)",
      "holds_original": true,
      "call_number": "CEN-1940",
      "medium_as_written": "bound enumeration books"
    },
    {
      "repository_name": "Example Records Online (made up publisher)",
      "holds_original": false,
      "medium_as_written": "digital images"
    }
  ],
  "coverage": {
    "places": [
      {
        "place": {
          "place_as_written": "Tumblebrook, Wrenshire, Erewhon"
        },
        "span": {
          "value": {
            "year": 1940
          },
          "as_written": "1940",
          "derivation": "interpreted"
        },
        "search_as": "Tumblebrook district 4"
      },
      {
        "place": {
          "place_as_written": "Larkspur hamlet, Wrenshire, Erewhon"
        },
        "span": {
          "value": {
            "year": 1940
          },
          "as_written": "1940",
          "derivation": "interpreted"
        },
        "search_as": "Tumblebrook district 4",
        "note": "Larkspur hamlet is filed with the Tumblebrook district in 1940."
      }
    ],
    "record_types": [
      "census_household"
    ],
    "languages": [
      "en"
    ],
    "span": {
      "value": {
        "year": 1940
      },
      "derivation": "interpreted"
    }
  },
  "link_status": "active",
  "last_verified_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
  "discovered_via": "manual",
  "created_by_task_id": "a90fb929-e2f7-5bc9-9d68-16e1f280bf3a",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

`source_url` becomes optional; the `provenance` block is dissolved (`status` → `link_status`,
`asserted_by` → `created_by_task_id`, `asserted_at` → `created_at`); `coverage.time_period`
becomes `coverage.span` (a date block, no year cap); places use the place block. Added:
`bibliographic` (title, creators, publisher, edition), `holdings` (which repository holds the
original), `is_living_flag` (required), a wider `source_type` list, `discovered_via`.

### Added in 2.1

- source_type (new field): 
- address (new field): MAXGEN 2.1 (G-14): where an archive or library is: its postal address in address_as_written, its town in place_as_written, and the MaxPlace in place_id; only on a source whose source_type is archive or library, or other for a church office, government office, cemetery, family papers or a private collection, and never a person's home address.

Episode 5, MaxSource — The routing brain (18:16): https://opengenealogyai.org/podcasts/audio/MAXGEN-05-maxsource.mp3 — Where records hide: coverage, access, provenance, and semantic search over sources. It describes MAXGEN v1.11; see https://opengenealogyai.org/changelog/#v20-2026-10-16 for what changed since.

## MaxPlace (MAXGEN 2.1 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxplace/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/place.schema.json  SHA-256 6940b499ea549f8314227906ae120f90fdc90e536e5824b5f34233a9c16fff4d
One MaxPlace is one real place with its history.

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- one MaxPlace document is one real place with its own history (its names, kinds, parent places and coordinates over time), each fact stored once as a claim with evidence so that many claims can point at it.

### Fields

- place_id (uuid, required): The place's permanent id: a random UUID created once by the writer (an import_file, resolve_conflict or build_tree task, R-24), never computed from a gazetteer or other outside id, and kept through renaming, re-typing an
- redistribution_license (licence, required): The licence under which this place document may be shared; when it is unclear, ask and never guess (RULES 7).
- name_assertions (array of name_claim, required): The names this place has had, at this level only (not the parent places), each a claim with its own evidence; at least one is required.
- kind_assertions (array of kind_claim): What kind of place this was over time (a territory that became a state, a village that became a city), each a dated claim with its own evidence.
- parent_place_assertions (array of parent_place_claim): The places this place lay inside over time, in one or more hierarchies (civil, church, judicial, census ...), each dated as closely as the evidence allows and each a claim with its own evidence; imported parents stay pro
- coordinate_assertions (array of coordinate_claim): Where this place is on the earth, each with an uncertainty radius and its own evidence; several are allowed for places that moved.
- related_place_assertions (array of related_place_claim): Links to other places this one was formed from, split from, merged into, succeeded or preceded, each a dated claim with its own evidence; a new county or a split is a new place, linked here.
- cited_record_ids (array of uuid): Records (MaxRecord ids) that are about the place as a whole, such as a parish history or a gazetteer page; research pointers kept beside the claims, each of which must exist (Appendix C).
- media_refs (array of media_ref): Maps and photographs of this place, pointed at by fingerprint on the record that holds each file (each file is described once, on the record that captured it).
- is_private (boolean): True hides this place from anything shareable; it can only rise (the helper refuses lowering it), and a small place (street, address, building, farm, estate or of no stated kind) that a possibly living person's live clai


### What changed from 1.13

A slim place authority: one real place with its names, kinds, parent places (dated, with
evidence) and coordinates (with their uncertainty when the evidence states one, never
invented) over time, related places (formed from, split from, merged into, succeeded by,
preceded by), gazetteer ids as outside ids, and undoable merges and `distinct_from`.
Every place claim cites evidence (a gazetteer page is saved as a record first). Made only by
import and analysis tasks.

## MaxGroup (MAXGEN 2.1 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgroup/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/group.schema.json  SHA-256 8dcdd51571717a6ae38eb9c6378ec0ae140423cd8999b548beee78045ba34657
One MaxGroup is one historical group (its own facts only; no member list).

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- one MaxGroup document is one historical group (an emigrant company, a regiment, a congregation, a household followed across documents) holding only the group's own facts, once, and no member list, because each membership is a claim on the person with group_id.

### Fields

- group_id (uuid, required): The group's permanent id: a random UUID created once by the writer (an import_file, resolve_conflict or build_tree task, R-24); merges and splits are made only by analysis (R-28).
- is_living_flag (boolean, required): Living A for the group file itself: true when its period or its names (such as 'the Mossbury household') touch someone who may be alive; when unsure, true; never worked out from members; a floor that only rises; true req
- redistribution_license (licence, required): The licence under which this group document may be shared; must be tier2-private when is_living_flag is true.
- group_kind (enum, required): What kind of historical group this is (there is no kind for a research cluster of friends, associates and neighbours: those stay as MaxTask results); when no value fits, write other and give the words in group_kind_as_wr
- group_kind_as_written (string): The source's or program's own words for the kind of group.
- group_kind_uri (uri): The address of the kind in a published vocabulary of group types, when there is one.
- name_assertions (array of name_claim, required): The names the group was known by, each a claim with its own evidence; at least one is required.
- fact_assertions (array of fact_claim): The group's own dated facts (organized, departed, arrived ...), each stored once here with its own evidence and never copied onto members; a member's page shows those inside the membership period at read time.
- parent_group_assertions (array of parent_group_claim): Larger groups this group belonged to during a period (a company inside a regiment), each a claim with its own evidence.
- observed_in (array of observed_in_item): The documents that describe the group, including ones that name none of its members.
- media_refs (array of media_ref): Photographs and other files of the group, pointed at by fingerprint on the record that holds each file (each file is described once, on the record that captured it).

### Example (made up; emigrant_company_no_members.json)

```json
{
  "group_id": "c2a6c59b-89f6-53e8-8b25-2775c40a9504",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "is_living_flag": false,
  "redistribution_license": "CC0",
  "group_kind": "emigrant_company",
  "name_assertions": [
    {
      "name_as_written": "Wrenshire Emigrant Company",
      "name_type": "as_recorded",
      "confidence": 0.9,
      "task_id": "06250dae-c716-5aaf-b0a6-2cd43fbedb65",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "19cda55a-513f-5558-a050-a093a7ae899d",
        "mention_id": "1",
        "record_event_ref": "e1",
        "quote": "Wrenshire Emigrant Company",
        "kind": "direct",
        "about": "other_mention",
        "note": "the company's name is written on each passenger's line"
      }
    }
  ],
  "fact_assertions": [
    {
      "fact_type": "departed",
      "date": {
        "value": {
          "year": 1853,
          "month": 5,
          "day": 10
        },
        "as_written": "10 May 1853"
      },
      "place": {
        "place_as_written": "Port Wren"
      },
      "occurrence_id": "d60f3769-33f4-5d95-a3e8-5c1805ff074c",
      "confidence": 0.9,
      "task_id": "06250dae-c716-5aaf-b0a6-2cd43fbedb65",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "7f41791d-0307-5469-91ae-7db589ef4f5c",
        "mention_id": "m1",
        "record_event_ref": "e1",
        "quote": "sailed from Port Wren on 10 May 1853",
        "kind": "direct",
        "about": "other_mention",
        "note": "the sailing is on the line that names the captain",
        "region_id": "8c2b92ab-1ff5-5b08-b24c-9cc7408f20bb"
      }
    }
  ],
  "observed_in": [
    {
      "record_id": "19cda55a-513f-5558-a050-a093a7ae899d",
      "record_event_ref": "e1"
    },
    {
      "record_id": "7f41791d-0307-5469-91ae-7db589ef4f5c",
      "record_event_ref": "e1",
      "note": "the journal names only the captain"
    }
  ],
  "created_by_task_id": "06250dae-c716-5aaf-b0a6-2cd43fbedb65",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

One historical group — an emigrant company, a regiment, a congregation, a household that
continued across documents — with its kind, its own names and dated facts, the larger groups it
belonged to, and the documents that describe it, once. **No member list:** a
membership is a claim on the person. FAN clusters (the friends, associates and neighbours
studied around one person) stay as MaxTask results. Made only by import and analysis tasks.

## MaxEvent (MAXGEN 2.1 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxevent/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/event.schema.json  SHA-256 1b69ee119e49ec2ecfaa10010017e93afec2fd79a6ac0e96f88e44c126cd2966
One MaxEvent is the identity of one occasion (thin).

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- the identity of one occasion (one baptism, one wedding, one voyage), kept thin: its permanent occurrence id, its ids in other programs, notes, pointers to the preferred versions and same-occasion merges. It never holds a participant list, the dates each document gives, copies of evidence, scores or its owner: who took part is worked out from role claims and mentions, and the owner is computed when read. Only the helper (one for every document event entry), importers and analysis tasks write it (R-24).

### Fields

- occurrence_id (uuid, required): This occasion's permanent id: a random UUID created once, by the helper when a record with event entries is stored or by the importer or analysis task that brings an outside event, and carried by every claim about the oc
- event_type (event_type, required): What kind of occasion this is; there is exactly one type per occurrence, so a licence and its ceremony never share an id.
- event_type_as_written (string): The document's or the other program's own words for the type, kept when event_type is other or when the words say more.
- type_uri (uri): A published vocabulary's address for the event type, when one exists.
- origin (origin, required): Where this occurrence came from: one document event entry, an outside program's event brought by an import, or an analysis.
- preferred (preferred): Pointers only to the claims that hold the preferred date and place and to the preferred order of versions; changed only under a resolve_conflict or build_tree task (R-24).
- conclusion_assertions (array of conclusion_claim): A reasoned conclusion that no single document states (a mine explosion dated between two reports), allowed only on an occurrence that an analysis created (origin.kind analysis) and changed only under a resolve_conflict o
- related (array of related_occurrence): Links to other occasions that an analysis concluded (a licence or banns for a wedding, part of a larger occasion, twins born together); changed only under a resolve_conflict or build_tree task.
- description_as_written (string): A description of the occasion exactly as a document or another program gives it (a GEDCOM 7 or Gramps event description).
- attributes (array of attribute): Facts about the occasion itself that another program kept as named attributes, word for word.
- media_refs (array of media_ref): Pictures or recordings of the occasion, pointing at saved copies that are described once on the records that captured them.
- is_private (boolean): True hides this occurrence from anything shareable; it only rises.
- is_living_flag (boolean, required): Living A floor, required with no default: true when any participant may be alive; unsure means true, the helper raises it and never lowers it, and the live answer is always computed at read time.
- redistribution_license (licence, required): Licence of this occurrence, raised by the helper and never lowered; a true is_living_flag requires tier2-private.

### Example (made up; marriage_shared_by_three_documents.json)

```json
{
  "occurrence_id": "d2631fcc-f683-56e1-bad4-590bf9a3d42d",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "event_type": "marriage",
  "origin": {
    "kind": "document_entry",
    "record_id": "da6ac270-29df-56f6-b577-cd764d5b1e2c",
    "record_event_ref": "e1"
  },
  "is_living_flag": false,
  "redistribution_license": "CC0",
  "preferred": {
    "date_assertion_id": "770b0a00-e2cc-58ec-9b18-bf5f6b06fc97",
    "order": [
      "770b0a00-e2cc-58ec-9b18-bf5f6b06fc97",
      "671ebcba-c400-52f8-ab02-9ca52f60aab4",
      "aeffecbc-3d5e-5b6a-b953-415869b10cf9"
    ],
    "set_by_task_id": "95284398-1483-57e3-98d3-af09efff15f5"
  },
  "merge_history": [
    {
      "merged_id": "185ca4ab-f08a-5983-8dff-4c25a3222303",
      "task_id": "95284398-1483-57e3-98d3-af09efff15f5",
      "merged_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
      "method": "same_occasion"
    },
    {
      "merged_id": "46b53474-91e1-5fad-b4a7-a28aeec234cf",
      "task_id": "95284398-1483-57e3-98d3-af09efff15f5",
      "merged_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
      "method": "same_occasion"
    }
  ],
  "created_by_task_id": "24408968-a56b-5a6c-a6f5-3a322540e24a",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

The identity of one occasion, thin: an occurrence id, its event type, where it came from
(`origin`: a record's event entry, an import, or an analysis), outside ids, notes, pointers to
the preferred date and place claims, links to related occasions, and same-occasion merges; an
occasion made by analysis may also carry a reasoned conclusion that no single document states,
citing an accepted proof. Made by the kit for every event entry on a record, and by importers
and analysis tasks. It holds no participant list and no copies of the dates documents give: who
took part is worked out from role claims.

### Listen

No episode yet: MaxEvent is new in MAXGEN 2.0.

## MaxName (MAXGEN 2.1 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxname/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/name.schema.json  SHA-256 521b1b28cfba2a121e40a9bb71b08982aa3bacba0d39a62907088c40606bacb1
One MaxName is knowledge about one name.

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxName is what is known about one name: its canonical form, its variants and cross-language cognates (each citing evidence and carrying the claim status ladder), and its phonetic keys.

### Fields

- name_id (uuid, required): This name record's own id: a random UUID created once by the writer and never reused.
- canonical_form (string, required): The modern standard spelling used as the anchor for every variant (such as the made-up surname Quillfeather), not necessarily English.
- canonical_script (script): The writing system of canonical_form.
- canonical_script_as_written (string): The writing system in the writer's own words, given when canonical_script is other.
- regional_canonical (array of object): Preferred forms of the name in other languages or regions, so no one language is the anchor.
- name_type (enum, required): What kind of name this is: given, surname, patronymic, matronymic, occupational, topographic, clan, byname, religious, title or other.
- name_type_as_written (string): The kind of name in the writer's own words, given when name_type is other.
- gender (enum): The gender the name is associated with in its own culture (a cultural association, never a statement about any person).
- gender_as_written (string): The association in the writer's own words, given when gender is other.
- language_of_origin (string): The language the name ultimately comes from, as an ISO 639-3 code.
- etymology (string): Where the name comes from and what it meant, written for a general reader.
- see_also_urls (array of string): Addresses of reference works about the name.
- variants (array of variant): Every known variant form; each is its own claim with evidence, retracted rather than deleted.
- phonetic_keys (object): Phonetic codes of the canonical form for fuzzy search, each with the algorithm version that made it so indexes rebuilt later do not mismatch silently.
- cognates (array of cognate): Related names in other languages; a first pass may name the target only by related_canonical_form and a later linking pass adds related_name_id.
- redistribution_license (licence, required): Whether this name record may be shared (unclear means ask, never guess).

### Example (made up; quillfeather_surname_variants_with_status.json)

```json
{
  "name_id": "32382ac8-1785-5e92-80a9-ff8e6bb9ad07",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "canonical_form": "Quillfeather",
  "name_type": "surname",
  "redistribution_license": "CC0",
  "canonical_script": "latin",
  "language_of_origin": "en",
  "etymology": "made up: 'a feather for a quill', an occupational byname for a scribe",
  "variants": [
    {
      "variant_id": "a59e46d3-9aa1-52ff-ba1e-dfd1fbc94515",
      "task_id": "234e98b3-972e-5af3-9071-e16b75c85474",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "8ee0b474-d41b-58eb-846a-9c707ff328cb",
        "mention_id": "m1",
        "quote": "Thaddeus Quillfeather",
        "kind": "direct"
      },
      "confidence": 0.4,
      "variant_text": "Quilfether",
      "variant_type": "spelling_variant",
      "language": "en",
      "script": "latin",
      "period_start": 1700,
      "period_end": 1800,
      "frequency": "rare"
    },
    {
      "variant_id": "ff446c8b-5e7a-5901-aea1-554d99dcf01f",
      "task_id": "81eff968-0e6a-51ba-9b5e-ec68e3e51fd2",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "a55282fa-e898-5089-88ec-e4fad4a18078",
        "mention_id": "30",
        "quote": "Quillfeather, Thaddeus",
        "kind": "direct"
      },
      "confidence": 0.9,
      "variant_text": "Quillfeather",
      "variant_type": "other",
      "variant_type_as_written": "the usual form",
      "frequency": "dominant",
      "status": "proposed",
      "asserted_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "phonetic_keys": {
    "soundex": {
      "value": "Q414",
      "algorithm_version": "american soundex"
    }
  },
  "cognates": [
    {
      "cognate_id": "e355716f-5a85-59fd-932d-5c27c9b221de",
      "task_id": "234e98b3-972e-5af3-9071-e16b75c85474",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "8ee0b474-d41b-58eb-846a-9c707ff328cb",
        "mention_id": "m1",
        "quote": "Thaddeus Quillfeather",
        "kind": "indirect"
      },
      "confidence": 0.3,
      "related_canonical_form": "Pennafeder",
      "relationship_type": "cross_language_cognate",
      "direction": "parallel_cognate",
      "notes": "made up"
    }
  ],
  "created_by_task_id": "487a3cb3-5656-5915-94ff-dcde58cbcbd9",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

The 1.13 shape is kept. `contributor` is removed (the task's provenance replaces it). Every
variant and cognate becomes a claim, with a kit-owned `assertion_id`, a status and a required
evidence link and confidence. Lifecycle fields added; `redistribution_license` required.

It describes MAXGEN v1.11; see https://opengenealogyai.org/changelog/#v20-2026-10-16 for what changed since.

## MaxRecognition (MAXGEN 2.1 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxrecognition/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/recognition.schema.json  SHA-256 ca72abecd356d4bee9bbc827c3213c231b95931d7884f9122ad744006e0f6e4e
One MaxRecognition is one machine reading of an image.

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxRecognition document is one machine reading (OCR of print or HTR of handwriting) of one image, kept with its per-word confidences so that readings of the same image can be compared; who or what made the reading is recorded on the task that produced it.

### Fields

- recognition_id (uuid, required): Random id of this reading, created once by its writer and never reused.
- recognition_type (enum, required): What kind of text was read: ocr for printed or typed text, htr for handwritten text, other (with recognition_type_as_written) for anything else.
- recognition_type_as_written (string): The reading program's own word for the kind of reading, written when recognition_type is other.
- image_url (uri): Address of the image that was read, never invented; at least one of image_url and raw_record_id is required.
- raw_record_id (uuid): The MaxRecord whose image this reading read; at least one of image_url and raw_record_id is required.
- copy_sha256 (sha256): Fingerprint of the saved copy that was read (described on raw_record_id, or on the live record that holds that copy), the same copy that evidence links cite.
- region_id (uuid): The marked region of that saved copy that was read, when only part of the image was read.
- output_text (string, required): The full text this reading produced, as plain text or as a JSON-encoded string of structured lines or words.
- processed_at (timestamp, required): When this reading was produced (UTC); renamed from the 1.x processing_date.
- language (lang): Language of the document that was read, as a language code such as de, la or en.
- confidence (confidence): Overall confidence the reader reported for the whole reading, 0 to 1, kept as reported and never computed by the kit.
- word_confidences (array of word_confidence): One item per word read, with its confidence, how it was produced, other readings considered and where it sits on the image.
- character_error_rate (number): Character error rate measured against a checked reference text, when one exists.
- word_error_rate (number): Word error rate measured against a checked reference text, when one exists.
- consensus_group_id (uuid): A grouping label shared by several readings of the same image so they can be compared; it names no MAXGEN document.
- redistribution_license (licence, required): Licence of this reading's text; tier2-private when the image is rights-restricted or anyone named may be alive.
- is_living_flag (boolean, required): Living A: true if anyone named in this reading may be alive, and true when unsure; a floor the kit only raises, and true requires tier2-private.
- attribution (attribution): Credit for a human transcriber or the organization that made the reading; a credit never sets a living flag.
- font_type (enum): Printed readings: the main kind of typeface on the page (other with font_type_as_written).
- font_type_as_written (string): The reader's own words for the typeface, written when font_type is other.
- scan_dpi (integer): Printed readings: the scan resolution of the image in dots per inch.
- script_type (enum): Handwritten readings: the handwriting script family of the document (other with script_type_as_written).
- script_type_as_written (string): The reader's own words for the script, written when script_type is other.
- approx_century (integer): Handwritten readings: the rough age of the handwriting as the first year of its century (1800 means the 1800s).
- searchable_variants (array of string): Every spelling this reading should be findable under, including uncertain readings and normalised forms.
- read_blind (boolean): MAXGEN 2.1 (G-30): true when the image was read before the reader saw any index or other reading of it, so the reading is independent; false when it was read after seeing one.
- based_on_recognition_id (uuid): MAXGEN 2.1 (G-30): the reading this one started from and corrected; what changed is worked out by comparing the two.
- field_comparison (array of field_comparison): MAXGEN 2.1 (G-11): how this reading compares with an index of the same image, field by field, as the reader judged it.

### Example (made up; htr_reading_with_region.json)

```json
{
  "recognition_id": "75d8a1f2-e917-5670-86e1-9b0072ede223",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "recognition_type": "htr",
  "raw_record_id": "a2834eea-1964-515d-8652-ff333819531c",
  "copy_sha256": "fbf7c8d29a52ddd03b3e453cb2dfe537a7b4961e8348a35c0718b614a098358f",
  "region_id": "48a16fee-ae07-5c81-850b-e8994524cbff",
  "output_text": "Bramblecott, Jesse | Head | M | 41 | Carter | Tumblebrook",
  "processed_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
  "language": "en",
  "confidence": 0.82,
  "word_confidences": [
    {
      "word": "Bramblecott",
      "char_offset": 0,
      "confidence": 0.91,
      "reading_type": "observed",
      "bbox": {
        "unit": "fraction",
        "x": 0.05,
        "y": 0.88,
        "w": 0.18,
        "h": 0.03,
        "page": 1
      }
    },
    {
      "word": "Carter",
      "char_offset": 39,
      "confidence": 0.62,
      "reading_type": "inferred_context",
      "inference_notes": "the occupation column is smudged",
      "alternatives": [
        {
          "text": "Carier",
          "confidence": 0.2
        }
      ],
      "bbox": {
        "unit": "px",
        "x": 1310,
        "y": 2210,
        "w": 160,
        "h": 44
      }
    }
  ],
  "character_error_rate": 0.04,
  "redistribution_license": "public-domain",
  "is_living_flag": false,
  "script_type": "latin_cursive",
  "approx_century": 1900,
  "searchable_variants": [
    "Bramblecot",
    "Bramblecott"
  ],
  "created_by_task_id": "873dd993-6a99-53c5-bbc8-25955efefaf9",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

The 1.13 fields are kept. `is_living_flag` added (required); `contributor` removed;
`image_url` and `raw_record_id` both optional but one required; `copy_sha256` and `region_id`
added (the same copy and region evidence cites); `processing_date` renamed `processed_at`;
`review_status`, `is_human_reviewed` and `is_independent` removed (reviews are tasks;
independence is computed).

### Added in 2.1

- field_comparison.field (new field): The field compared, as written (name, age, birthplace ...).
- field_comparison.index_value (new field): What the index says.
- field_comparison.mention_ref (new field): Which person or line of the index the field belongs to, as the reader wrote it.
- field_comparison.page_value (new field): What the image says, as read.
- field_comparison.result (new field): The image and the index agree, differ, or the image is unclear there.
- based_on_recognition_id (new field): MAXGEN 2.1 (G-30): the reading this one started from and corrected; what changed is worked out by comparing the two.
- field_comparison (new field): MAXGEN 2.1 (G-11): how this reading compares with an index of the same image, field by field, as the reader judged it.
- read_blind (new field): MAXGEN 2.1 (G-30): true when the image was read before the reader saw any index or other reading of it, so the reading is independent; false when it was read after seeing one.

### Listen

Episode 6, MaxRecognition — Teaching machines to read (25:21): https://opengenealogyai.org/podcasts/audio/MAXGEN-06-maxrecognition.mp3 — OCR and handwriting provenance, word-level confidence, labelled inference, and consensus. It describes MAXGEN v1.11; see https://opengenealogyai.org/changelog/#v20-2026-10-16 for what changed since.

## MaxDNA (MAXGEN 2.1 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxdna/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/dna.schema.json  SHA-256 dc96f9d4d08b8c484a8fb1ac5d8c7a6ae6ffb9e623817fc14b99d63567986bf7
One MaxDNA is one person's DNA test and its matches (always private).

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxDNA document is one person's DNA test and its matches, always tier2-private, holding no raw genotype data and no raw kit number (only keyed fingerprints), with each match a claim that cites the saved match list.

### Fields

- dna_id (uuid, required): Random id of this DNA test document, created once by its writer and never reused.
- person_id (uuid, required): The MaxPerson who took this test (the one top-level key MaxDNA shares with MaxPerson; the kind is decided by dna_id first).
- test_type (enum, required): Type of DNA test: unknown when the source does not say (an imported DNA table may not), other with test_type_as_written.
- test_type_as_written (string): The source's own words for the test type, written when test_type is other.
- test_provider (enum): Company or platform that performed or hosts the original test (other with test_provider_as_written).
- test_provider_as_written (string): The source's own name for the provider, written when test_provider is other.
- test_date (date): When the test was taken, as a date block (a year alone is fine).
- kit_id_status (enum): Whether the kit number's fingerprint is known: hashed (the default when left out) requires kit_id_hash; unknown when the source gave no kit number.
- kit_id_hash (sha256): Keyed fingerprint (HMAC-SHA-256 keyed with the database's own secret kit_key, not a plain SHA-256) of the kit number, trimmed and upper-cased; the kit makes it with `maxgen_db.py kit-hash`; the raw kit number is never st
- kit_source (string, required): Where this test's details came from, in plain words (for example user_self_report, opensnp_public or an imported tree file).
- haplogroup_y (string): Y-DNA haplogroup (paternal line) as the provider reported it, for example R-M269.
- haplogroup_mt (string): mtDNA haplogroup (maternal line) as the provider reported it, for example H1a1.
- haplogroup_y_confidence (confidence): The provider's own confidence in the Y-DNA haplogroup, 0 to 1, kept as reported.
- haplogroup_mt_confidence (confidence): The provider's own confidence in the mtDNA haplogroup, 0 to 1, kept as reported.
- ancestry_composition (array of ancestry_component): Ethnicity or admixture estimates as the provider reported them; they add up to about 100 percent.
- endogamy_flag (boolean): True if the test subject belongs to an endogamous population, where the usual shared-cM ranges are unreliable.
- endogamy_population (string): The endogamous population, in plain words, when endogamy_flag is true.
- matches (array of match): The matches reported for this test, each a claim citing the saved match list; a match between two tests in this database is stored once, on the test with the smaller dna_id (R-25).
- kit_aliases (array of kit_alias): The same kit's ids at other services, as keyed fingerprints only (replaces the 1.x external_ids map).
- is_living_flag (boolean, required): Living A: true if the test subject may be alive, and true when unsure; a floor the kit only raises.
- redistribution_license (licence, required): Always tier2-private: genetic data touches relatives who never agreed to share it, so no other value is accepted.
- raw_genotype_stored (const false, required): Always false: MAXGEN never stores raw genotype data (FASTQ, VCF or raw SNP files); that stays with the provider or the person.
- external_raw_data_location (string): Plain words saying where the raw data is held (for example the person's own drive or the provider account); never a raw kit number, a genotype or an unhashed id.
- consent_status (enum, required): Legal basis for keeping this DNA data: the first four values are consent; withdrawn, pending, unknown (an import that does not say) and any value the kit does not know are read as not consented, so the test is shown only
- consented_at (timestamp): When consent was given.
- consent_evidence_url (uri): Address of the signed consent record, kept somewhere private.
- withdrawal_requested_at (timestamp): When the test subject asked for this DNA data to be withdrawn.
- source_record_ids (array of uuid): MaxRecords that document this test (a saved provider page, a consent form, a lab report); replaces the 1.x source_records.

### Example (made up; autosomal_with_match_ids.json)

```json
{
  "dna_id": "57dbf476-5888-5045-a13a-c372f2e9b13c",

      "shared_cm": 212,
      "triangulated_with": [
        "80852453-d847-594d-8108-32c258b9cb7d"
      ],
      "confidence": 0.9,
      "task_id": "c0daf871-47b4-5ba0-b433-ca99d0ca5c74",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "4a8c78ae-4fc4-5e3a-9e5d-e85304a6b303",
        "mention_id": "m2",
        "quote": "Penhallow, S. | 212 cM",
        "kind": "direct"
      }
    }
  ],
  "source_record_ids": [
    "4a8c78ae-4fc4-5e3a-9e5d-e85304a6b303"
  ],
  "kit_aliases": [
    {
      "system": "gedmatch",
      "id_hash": "acd86c98e75eed5b73b53e7600ba819ed7482b29687618786aa49ceacdef7f81"
    }
  ],
  "created_by_task_id": "c0daf871-47b4-5ba0-b433-ca99d0ca5c74",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

The 1.13 fields are kept, always `tier2-private`. `asserted_by` and `asserted_at` removed; the
top-level `notes` string replaced by the shared notes list; `kit_id_hash` optional with `kit_id_status`; `test_date` a
date block; `external_ids` becomes `kit_aliases`; `source_records` becomes `source_record_ids`.
Each match becomes a claim with a permanent `match_id`, its own `is_living`, and evidence citing
the saved match list (a `dna_match_list` record, which the schema keeps living and
`tier2-private`); predicted relationships keep the company's own words and probabilities. A
match between two tests in one database is stored once. Kit numbers are never stored: their
fingerprints are keyed with a secret only the person's own database holds.

### Listen

Episode 4, MaxDNA — Genetic evidence without giving up privacy (23:23): https://opengenealogyai.org/podcasts/audio/MAXGEN-04-maxdna.mp3 — Hashed kit IDs, consent, endogamy, phasing, and how DNA boosts documentary confidence. It describes MAXGEN v1.11; see https://opengenealogyai.org/changelog/#v20-2026-10-16 for what changed since.
